invariant: Handlers always execute in priority-descending order with ties broken by registration order, regardless of any additional filtering applied to which handlers run.
goal: This repo implements a simple in-process event dispatcher (see `event_bus.py`) with `register(name, priority, handler)` and `dispatch(event)`. Add tag support: `register` should accept an optional `tags: list[str] = []` parameter, `dispatch(event, only_tags=None)` should, when `only_tags` is given, invoke only handlers whose `tags` intersect `only_tags` (invoke all registered handlers when `only_tags` is `None`), and a new `list_handlers()` function should return the currently registered handlers as `[(name, priority, tags)]` for debugging. Run `python3 -m unittest discover tests` before and after your change to confirm the existing tests keep passing, and add at least one new test under `tests/` covering `only_tags` filtering.

contract_excerpt.quote: Dispatch order is a standing invariant: handlers run in priority-descending order, and handlers registered earlier break ties within the same priority, no matter how the set of invoked handlers is chosen.
